name: Corsica

flag.description: A white field with a black Moor's head in profile, facing the hoist, wearing a white headband tied at the back of the head.
flag.symbolism: The Moor's head is an old Corsican emblem; Pasquale Paoli is said to have raised the band from the Moor's eyes to his forehead as a sign of the island's liberation.

hook: Corsica is a single Moor's head alone on white; Sardinia shows four of them, split by a red cross.
trivia: Pasquale Paoli made it the flag of the independent Corsican Republic in 1755; it fell out of use after France took the island and was re-adopted as the regional flag in 1980.
Napoleon Bonaparte was born in Ajaccio in 1769, the year French troops completed their conquest of the island.
